text.p: Samsonite Corp. said Thursday it would cut 450 jobs, or about 6 percent of its work force, in a restructuring that will include a one-time charge of $10.7 million.
The world's largest luggage manufacturer said it expected pretax savings of $12.7 million from the consolidation of operations in North America but in Europe and the Far East.
It said it would consolidate production of hard luggage at its biggest domestic plant in Denver and also eventually move many administrative functions to its headquarters city.
About a third of the jobs to be cut are outside the United States and about two-thirds are managerial, office, and clerical positions, Samonsite said.
It currently employs about 8,000 people worldwide.
Since it expects to complete the restructuring within the next year, most of the anticipated annual savings will take effect starting in November 1997.
Samsonite stock rose 25 cents to $33.75 on Nasdaq. The announcement came after the close of regular trading.
